notes:
Overview:
- SilverQuill builds JetBrains IDE plugins (IntelliJ + PyCharm) that provide local-indexed code completions + an optional cloud-backed copilot. Targeting developer teams inside mid-market and enterprise ISVs.
- Core differentiator: Rust-based local indexer for workspace, low-latency streaming completions (<50ms target median), offline-first completion engine, and explicit model/version pinning in the plugin.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2026-01-12: Intro call (AE Diego) — product overview, marketplace distribution plan. Customer: "we need local index, cloud only is non-starter for some customers."
- 2026-01-28: Demo (screen share) of local indexer on 200-file Java monorepo (ff_2026-02-18_8342). Observed warm-completion latencies ~30-45ms on dev laptop.
- 2026-02-10: Sent security packet + SOC2 evidence (drive:/security/silverquill/sec-answers-2026-02-20.md).
- 2026-02-18: Deep technical call with infra + SRE (Priya present). Discussed on-prem installer, KMS integration, and audit log schema. (ff_2026-02-18_8342)
- 2026-02-25: Shared preliminary POC plan and perf targets; engineering asked for model-pin and fallback to quantized 8-bit variant. (gmail_thread_4M1xq0Z)
- 2026-03-02: Contracting call — legal wants to see on-prem licensing terms and installer validation steps.

Use-case & requirements summary:
- Primary workload: interactive code completion + assistant actions inside IntelliJ/PyCharm.
- Secondary: code search + embeddings used for fuzzy symbol lookup.
- Latency target: median <50ms for inline completions; 95th <150ms for streaming multi-line suggestions.
- Throughput: expect ~150 active developers in pilot, concurrency burst to ~50 completions/sec.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay for predictable pricing for dedicated pools or private install but need clear unit economics for token-heavy features.
- Model preferences: prefer open-model variants with pinned versions; want Redwood to support pinning at plugin and server level (plugin declares allowed versions).
- Routing/fallback: primary local index + local quantized model; fallback to dedicated/private cloud model for large-context completions.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO (SAML), audit logs with developer identifiers, optional on-prem data residency for EU customers, KMS/HSM for key management.

Evaluation / POC plan (success criteria):
- Deliverable: on-prem installer + small private control plane deployed in SilverQuill staging VPC.
- Perf: inline completion median <50ms across 3 representative repos; 95th <150ms.
- Quality: completion accept rate within 5% of baseline (current internal engine).
- Ops: plugin can pin model v1.3.4 and roll back to v1.3.2 via Redwood control plane.
- Security: SAML SSO + audit logs delivered to their SIEM.

Technical notes & dev feedback:
- Plugin requires an agent on developer machine for the local indexer. Agent telemetry accepted but must honor opt-out per dev.
- Developer requested streaming over SSE for minimal overhead; we discussed gRPC/TCP option for private installs.
- They care about KV cache TTL semantics — want deterministic cache invalidation on repo changes.
- Asked about Redwood Optimize: interested in batching suggestions across idle editors to reduce token spend.

Procurement & commercial:
- Estimate ARR ask: $60k-$120k for 12 months with staged rollout.
- Legal wants standard EULA + separate on-prem license + acceptance tests for installer.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-15: Infra handoff call (Priya + infra) to start private control plane deploy in staging VPC.
- Provide installer acceptance checklist and sample model pinning manifest. (owner: Diego)
- Run perf baseline week of 2026-03-22 on two customer repos.

Open blockers (short):
- Security sign-off on on-prem installer (SEC review still open).
- Need perf proof vs their baseline on two large monorepos.
- Finance needs final pricing approval for enterprise seat tier.

Quoted lines from customer:
- "If we can't run fully offline or in our VPC, we won't push to enterprise customers."
- "Model pinning in the plugin is a must — our QA needs stable reproducible completions."
